Done — out of practice runs. Final solution.py summary:

A Triton grouped-GEMM MoE up-projection with fused SwiGLU epilogue. Each program handles one (128×BN) tile of one expert and computes both GEMMs (gate and up) sharing A-tile loads, then applies silu(gate)*up in fp32 before the bf16 store. The variable-length expert schedule (tile→expert, row start, valid rows, total tiles) is built on-GPU with torch tensor ops (searchsorted over cumulative tile counts), so forward() has no host sync and handles ragged/empty experts; L2-swizzled program ordering; a TMA tensor-descriptor kernel is the primary path with automatic fallback to a classic pointer-based kernel if Triton lacks the API (warp-specialization was tried but crashes Triton's MLIR pipeline on sm120, so it's disabled).

Verified remotely: `status: correct` (all 3 shapes, seeds, ragged stress cases PASS), benchmark ~19.7 ms / 0.65 ms / 13.8 ms on the three shapes (~42/53/40 tflops by the harness's metric, peak_fraction 0.089 — graded LOW, but correct and the fastest of my iterations).
